title: A copper busbar heating up under 200 A in still air, written as two fields (demonstration)

provenance.purpose: the kernel's own equations in time: an electric potential and a temperature, coupled both ways (the Joule heat warms the bar, the warm copper conducts less); nothing about busbars is programmed. A demonstration, not checked against a measurement (tools/kerneltest.c K11 to K13 check the pieces against exact solutions)
provenance.material: copper: electrical conductivity 58.0 MS/m at 20 C and its temperature coefficient of resistance 0.00393 /K, the International Annealed Copper Standard (IEC 60028); density 8933 kg/m^3, specific heat 385 J/(kg K), thermal conductivity 401 W/(m K) for pure copper at 300 K (Incropera and DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, table A.1)
provenance.assumptions: still air exchanges 10 W/(m^2 K) with every face, a typical value assumed for a small bar, not measured; the bar's ends are insulated terminals; radiation is left out

copper.source: IEC 60028 (electrical); Incropera and DeWitt, table A.1 (thermal)

controls.label: the current density at the end, A/m^2 (200 A is 6.67e6)
